transcript.text: Good morning, everyone. Thank you for joining this review session. As you know, we have 12 students who need to complete the medication-safety simulation assessment this term, and I've received a draft plan that I'd like us to go through together before I give my final approval. The draft proposes using a faculty evaluator, two rotations of six students, an assessment date of May 8, 2027, and a results-entry date of June 21, 2027. I'd like to hear from each of you — clinical coordinator, simulation-lab manager, registrar, and student-services coordinator — on whether you see any issues with this plan so we can make sure everything is in order before it goes into the academic calendar.
transcript.speaker: A1

transcript.text: I need to flag a compliance issue with the draft plan. During this month's clinical-compliance review, I confirmed that the state nursing board's current medication-simulation rule requires the evaluator to be a current, unencumbered registered nurse. However, the draft plan only specifies 'faculty evaluator' without stating this RN requirement. We need to update the language to reflect the state board's rule before this plan moves forward.
transcript.speaker: A2

transcript.text: I need to flag an equipment and safety issue with the draft plan. I completed the equipment check yesterday, and only three of our medication pumps have current calibration certificates. Our lab's safety procedure limits each pump rotation to three students. The draft plan currently calls for two rotations of six students, which would exceed the safety limit of three students per pump rotation. We need to revise the rotation count before this plan can move forward.
